title: Multiplying Two Two-Digit Numbers
short: Find four partial products and add them.
trouble: Children multiply only tens by tens and ones by ones, so 23 × 14 becomes 212.

blocks.html: Now both factors have two digits. The area model still works: split both numbers by place value, and the rectangle has four parts.
For $23 \times 14$, split $23 = 20 + 3$ and $14 = 10 + 4$. Find all four partial products: tens × tens, tens × ones, ones × tens and ones × ones. Then add them.
Each part of 23 must be multiplied by each part of 14, because the whole rectangle is $23$ by $14$. Cutting it both ways makes four rectangles. Leave one out and you lose part of the area.

blocks.title: Bigger digits
steps: Estimate: about $50 \times 35 = 1{,}750$. Close, so the answer is reasonable.

blocks.html: Multiplying only tens by tens and ones by ones: $2 \times 1 = 2$ and $3 \times 4 = 12$, written as "212". That skips two of the four parts. Check with an estimate: $23 \times 14$ is about $20 \times 15 = 300$, so 212 is too small.
